question: Is there a word every language shares?
answer: Possibly one. "Huh?" — the sound for signalling you did not catch something — appears in essentially every language studied, with a strikingly similar form. It looks less like a word inherited from a common ancestor and more like one every language independently converges on, because conversation needs it.
move: Every language on record has its own version of "huh?", and they all sound alike.
